errors.english: Whichever word it depends upon, one must infer "from that cause."
errors.why: གང་གི་སྒྲ is 'the word "which" (yat)': because of the relative 'which', the correlative 'from that cause' must be supplied; it is not 'whichever word'.

errors.english: The phrase "at that time" should be placed first, depending on whichever word is used
errors.why: What is put first is 'that cause' (supplied because of the relative 'which'), and the whole is construed with 'would be the property of all'; 'at that time' is the lemma, not the thing moved forward.

errors.english: Even if any particular humor like wind were the cause, not every particular instance would possess all forms of desire and so forth.
errors.why: The whole passage from གལ་ཏེ ('even if any particular of wind etc. is the cause... because it has a definite auxiliary') is the anticipated objection introduced by 'But the result...', not the commentator's own statement.

errors.english: This is because the error is the same.
errors.why: འཁྲུལ་པ here is the logical 'deviation' (vyabhicāra) of the inference, which is equally present, not a generic 'error'.

note: Follows the gloss-by-gloss commentary in outline, but misreads the syntactic glosses on the relative-correlative and blurs where the anticipated objection begins.

errors.english: the cowherd's mother will come to know through unrest
errors.why: ཞི་བ is the name Śāntā/Śānti (the person whose hand throws the curd pot just below), or at most 'calm'; 'unrest' reads it as its opposite.

errors.english: means that the result is the curd ladle thrown
errors.why: The commentary marks a range of the root text, from 'You and the cowherd's...' up to '...that fruit of the curd pot falling on the head'; it does not say the first phrase means the second.
ཚང here is 'nest', glossed on the next side as 'a dwelling', not 'complete'.

note: Mostly a serviceable rendering of a lemma-and-gloss commentary, but the Śāntī episode is misconstrued and one lemma is mistranslated.

errors.english: Whatever is desired, make that specific.
errors.why: Both pādas are root verse ('If you say not every statement is intended, qualify the one that is intended'); the first pāda has been absorbed into prose.
བསྒྲུབ་བྱ་སྒྲུབ་པར་བྱེད་པ is 'what proves the probandum' (sādhyasādhana), not establishing through the probandum.

note: A good grasp of the argument about qualifying the reason and of the general rule and exception, with a verse pāda merged into prose and one slip in the logic vocabulary.

errors.english: When the words reached their conclusion
errors.why: The gods' acclamation ('well done, O king!') spread to the ends of the directions (Skt. dikprānta-); it is not that 'the words reached their conclusion'.

note: A faithful and readable verse rendering of the Tibetan; the opening line misreads the cry spreading to the ends of the directions.

errors.why: The consequence that follows ('if there are no beings, for whom compassion?') is the opponent's objection to the no-self thesis; a note that speaks of a 'proper view of the self' misleads.

note: A sound rendering of the past, present and future mind argument and the plantain simile; only the last bracketed note is misleading.

errors.english: does not wear the robes belonging to the (Sangha) the monastic community
errors.why: བགོ here is 'distribute, share out' (cf. the preceding rule about not distributing in the rain without a roof); the passage is about distributing the Saṅgha's cloth, not wearing robes, and the same misreading recurs in 'if they do not wear them'.

fix.find: does not wear the robes belonging to the (Sangha) the monastic community
fix.replace: does not distribute the cloth belonging to the (Sangha) the monastic community

errors.english: (Upali) the Buddha's disciple foremost in knowledge of monastic law replied, "They should be given."
errors.why: Upāli asks the question ('Venerable, ...?') and the Buddha answers addressing him: 'Upāli, it should be given'; Upāli is not the one who replies.

fix.find: (Upali) the Buddha's disciple foremost in knowledge of monastic law replied, "They should be given."
fix.replace: The Buddha replied, "Upāli, they should be given."

errors.english: the son will not return as the master of the father's house
errors.why: The reason given for accepting is that the expelled son does not cease to be an owner of the father's house; the English says the opposite.

fix.find: the son will not return as the master of the father's house
fix.replace: the son does not cease to be an owner of the father's house

errors.english: it is entrusted to the primary trusted figures
errors.why: གཏམས་པ here means the phrase 'given or taken by a relative' is included under (counted among) the trusted principals, father, mother and so on; nothing is entrusted.

note: The Vinaya procedure is misread at several points: distributing is rendered as wearing, Upāli is made the one who answers, and the reason about the expelled son is reversed.

errors.english: the howling lords of those who commit unwholesome deeds inflict suffering
errors.why: The doers of unwholesome deeds are the ones crying out, pitiable with their wails of suffering (continued on the next side); they are not tormentors who inflict suffering.

note: An effective rendering of the verses on desire for another man's wife; one clause at the end turns the suffering beings into their tormentors.
A faithful rendering of the Akṣayamati citation on right view and right thought and of the passage on the instantaneous abandonment of latencies.
An accurate rendering of the sequence of faith and of the spiritual friend's instruction for making faith firm.
A literal and stiff rendering of a dense Vinaya passage on the first saṃghāvaśeṣa; obscure phrases are rendered word for word rather than clarified, but no confident errors of substance.
